Macrons

Consonantal i

Theme

Common words: verbs, qualities & ideas

normal adjective

also usual, it’s normal, as normal, back to normal, customary, natural (to be expected), it’s only natural

classical

Cic. Verr. 2.5.117: ūsitātum est (Lewis & Short)
Caes. BG 7.22: nōtum atque ūsitātum (Lewis & Short)
Traupman 299: current, in general use, ūsitātus

ūsitātus, ūsitāta, ūsitātum

adjective

normal, usual, customary, ordinary

“That’s normal” is ūsitātum est, or with a verb ita fierī solet. Back to normal: in prīstinum statum redīre (Caes. BG 7.54; see former).

Examples

  • fēcit statim, ut fit, fastīdium cōpia

    as normally happens, plenty soon bred boredomLiv. 3.1.7

  • semel hic cessāvit et, ut fit, in scālīs latuit

    once he played truant and, as boys will, hid on the stairsHor. Ep. 2.2.14–15

Other words

  • solitus, solita, solitum — usual, accustomed

    participle of soleō, used as an adjective · also used · classical · Liv. 3.38.9: quod solitum quicquam līberae cīvitātis fieret (Lewis & Short); Ov. M. 7.84: solitō fōrmōsior (Lewis & Short); Traupman 401: usual, solitus

    Augustan and later, not in Cicero or Caesar (Lewis & Short). With a comparative, solitō is “than usual”: solitō fōrmōsior, better-looking than usual.

  • ut fit — as normally happens

    phrase · also used · classical · Liv. 3.1.7: fēcit statim, ut fit, fastīdium cōpia; Hor. Ep. 2.2.14–15

  • normālis, normāle — made by the square, at right angles

    adjective, third declension · avoid · classical · Quint. 11.3.141: normālis angulus, a right angle (Lewis & Short); M-O s.v. normal, ordinary, average (marked as a modern sense; Grosse 1846)

    From norma, a carpenter’s square. The sense “normal” is nineteenth-century medical Latin (pulsūs frequentia normālis, Grosse 1846, in Morgan–Owens).

See also as usual, practice, average, natural, common.

SourcesLewis & Short: usitatus · Lewis & Short: usitor · Lewis & Short: soleo · Lewis & Short: fio · Lewis & Short: normalis
